n3bfc2a7cad5.s: The earliest literary reference to the Andhras occurs in the:
n3bfc2a7cad5.x: The Aitareya Brahmana gives the earliest literary reference to the Andhras, in the story of Sunahshepa and Vishwamitra's disowned sons.

nap-history-1-29.s: The inscription in which the Kakatiyas were mentioned for the first time is the:
nap-history-1-29.x: The Magallu inscription is the first to mention the Kakatiyas; Kalamalla is the first Telugu inscription.

n6e5050b8118.s: Which source is regarded as the most reliable for ancient Indian history?
n6e5050b8118.x: Inscriptions are regarded as the most reliable source; foreign accounts only supplement them where Indian texts are silent.

n9292463d004.x: Mortimer Wheeler excavated Arikamedu in 1945; Marshall worked at Mohenjodaro, Rea at Bhattiprolu and Longhurst at Nagarjunakonda.

n170341d4802.s: Tamil-Brahmi rock inscriptions at Mangulam, Sittanavasal and Arittapatti lie in which region?
n170341d4802.x: Mangulam, Sittanavasal and Arittapatti are Tamil-Brahmi rock inscription sites in the Pandya region.

n8f9de110ffb.s: The Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts of Ashoka are written in which script?
n8f9de110ffb.x: Kharosthi, a right-to-left script of north-western India, is represented in the Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts.

n59431648c1a.s: Which inscription contains the first edict naming Ashoka as 'Asoka'?
n59431648c1a.x: The Maski inscription is the first edict that names Ashoka as 'Asoka'; it also uses the term Gulmika.

n560144dd592.s: The Milindapanho records a dialogue between Menander and:
n560144dd592.x: The Milindapanho records the dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander and the monk Nagasena.

nindian-history-1-59.s: According to the Hathigumpha inscription, Kharavela followed which religion?
nindian-history-1-59.x: The Hathigumpha inscription opens with a salute to the Jinas, showing that Kharavela was a Jain.

nindian-history-30-15.s: Who is known as 'Padakavita Pitamaha', the earliest known Telugu song-composer?
nindian-history-30-15.x: Annamacharya, called Padakavita Pitamaha, is the earliest known Telugu song-composer.

nindian-history-1-95.s: Rudradaman repaired which lake without forced labour, as recorded in the Junagadh inscription?
nindian-history-1-95.x: The Junagadh inscription at Girnar records that Rudradaman repaired the Sudarshana lake without forced labour.

nindian-history-54-18.s: Which foreign visitor wrote on Hindu religion, the Puranas, Sanskrit and Yoga?
nindian-history-54-18.x: Al-Biruni wrote on Hindu learning; I-Tsing wrote on Buddhist relics and Fa-Hien on Buddhist pilgrimage.

nd8554cf6621.s: The Samarangana Sutradhara was written by:
nd8554cf6621.x: The Samarangana Sutradhara was written by King Bhoja, not Pravarasena II.

nc3914a64dc8.x: The Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa are Sri Lankan Pali chronicles that illuminate Mauryan history and Andhra Buddhism.

nee7ec6395d2.s: The Nasik Prashasti, which hails Gautamiputra Satakarni as destroyer of the Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas, was composed by:
nee7ec6395d2.x: The Nasik Prashasti was composed by Gautami Balashri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni.

n2bca626a6bb.s: According to the Puranas, the last Satavahana ruler was:
n2bca626a6bb.x: The Puranas name Pulomavi III, not Gautamiputra Satakarni, as the last Satavahana.

nindian-history-97-19.x: Rajasekhara wrote Kavyamimamsa; Kalidasa was the great Sanskrit poet of the Gupta age.

nindian-history-54-12.s: Which foreign visitor wrote about the Brahmins and Shramanas?
nindian-history-54-12.x: Megasthenes wrote of Brahmins and Shramanas; Fa-Hien wrote of Buddhist pilgrimage and Hiuen-Tsang of Mahayana and Nalanda.

nindian-history-97-20.s: Kavirajamarga is attributed to which ruler?
nindian-history-97-20.x: Kavirajamarga is attributed to the Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I.

n80fdff95bae.s: 'Natural History' was written in Latin by:
n80fdff95bae.x: Pliny wrote Natural History in Latin; Ptolemy wrote Geography and the Periplus was by an anonymous Greek sailor.

neddd22a8405.s: In stratigraphy, the principle that lower layers are older than the layers above them is called:
neddd22a8405.x: This principle is superposition; counting annual tree rings is dendrochronology.

n73e7e4b2794.s: Mudrarakshasa and Devichandraguptam were written by:
n73e7e4b2794.x: Both plays were written by Vishakhadatta; Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita.

nindian-history-1-12.s: The Ayodhya inscription is associated with:
nindian-history-1-12.x: The Ayodhya inscription is associated with Pushyamitra Shunga; Nashik is linked with Gautamiputra Satakarni and Hathigumpha with Kharavela.

nf2b96e56b12.s: The Bhattiprolu inscription refers to which body?
nf2b96e56b12.x: The Bhattiprolu inscription refers to a Nigama-sabha (guild assembly).

nc7fd32be5b6.s: The Boghaz-Koi inscription, which names Indra, Varuna, Mitra and Nasatya, belongs to the:
nc7fd32be5b6.x: The Boghaz-Koi inscription from Asia Minor belongs to the fourteenth century BC, not the fourth.

n559deae064c.s: The Junagadh inscription was issued by:
n559deae064c.x: The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I is a long Sanskrit inscription recording the repair of the Sudarshana lake.

n090643217f8.s: Masulia, mentioned by Ptolemy as an eastern trading centre, is identified with:
n090643217f8.x: Ptolemy's Masulia is identified with Machilipatnam, an important trading centre on the eastern side.

n36ceb6bfe7a.s: Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in which language?
n36ceb6bfe7a.x: Kitab-ul-Hind was written in Arabic, not Persian.

n39135fca53d.s: The Bhattiprolu stupa was excavated by:
n39135fca53d.x: Alexander Rea excavated the Bhattiprolu stupa; Robert Sewell wrote A Forgotten Empire.

n40d2556cd0b.s: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in:

n127bbde64a3.s: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela was composed in which language?
n127bbde64a3.x: The Hathigumpha inscription was composed in Prakrit using the Brahmi script.

nc50b98533f9.x: Banabhatta's Harshacharita refers to Yajna Sri Satakarni as Trisamudradheesvara.

ndc2a11d1246.x: Gunadhya composed Brihatkatha in Paisachi; it is a source for the Satavahana age.

n2be392430de.s: Ship-motif coins are associated with which Satavahana ruler?
n2be392430de.x: Ship-motif coins, evidence of maritime trade, are associated with Yajna Sri Satakarni (and Vasishthiputra Pulumavi); Gautamiputra is known for re-striking Nahapana's coins.

n12a9907b2e5.s: The first definite references to coins such as kahapana, nikkha, kamsa and kakanika occur in:
n12a9907b2e5.x: Pali texts give the first definite references to these coins, corroborated by punch-marked coins.

n3fe3921c3d1.s: Andhranagari, mentioned in the Bhimasena and Serivanija Jatakas, is identified with:
n3fe3921c3d1.x: Andhranagari is identified with Dhanyakataka; P. C. Ray identified its river as the Krishna.

n7625951a33d.s: Sangam texts are dated to about:
n7625951a33d.x: Sangam texts are dated to about the 3rd century BCE - 3rd century CE and describe the Chera, Chola and Pandya kingdoms.

nindian-history-30-9.s: The earliest known copper plate in India is the:
nindian-history-30-9.x: The Sohgaura plate is the earliest known copper plate and the earliest royal famine-related order.

nindian-history-54-17.s: The Chinese pilgrim I-Tsing is associated with the period:

nap-history-14-5.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler gave away crores of gold coins?
nap-history-14-5.x: The Ikshvaku Santamula I gave away crores of gold coins.

nindian-history-1-32.s: The Rabatak inscription (discovered 1993) is in the Bactrian language written in which script?
nindian-history-1-32.x: The Rabatak inscription is in Bactrian written in the Greek script.

nindian-history-1-13.s: The Sarnath Buddhist image inscription dated 81 AD is associated with:
nindian-history-1-13.x: The Sarnath Buddhist image inscription is dated to Kanishka's third year (81 AD).

nindian-history-1-29.s: Which inscription from Bengal deals with famine relief?
nindian-history-1-29.x: The Mahasthan inscription in Bengal deals with famine relief.

nindian-history-1-58.s: The earliest long Sanskrit inscription and an early specimen of the Kavya style is the:
nindian-history-1-58.x: The Junagadh inscription is the earliest long Sanskrit inscription and an early Kavya-style work.

nindian-history-54-4.s: Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of:
nindian-history-54-4.x: Fa-Hien came to India during the reign of Chandragupta II.

nindian-history-1-80.s: The Aihole inscription, written in Southern Brahmi, is in which language?
nindian-history-1-80.x: The Aihole inscription is in Sanskrit and uses the Southern Brahmi script.

nindian-history-1-37.s: According to the Aihole inscription, Pulakeshin II stopped Harsha's southward advance at the:
nindian-history-1-37.x: The Aihole inscription, composed by Ravikirti, says Pulakeshin II stopped Harsha at the Narmada, not the Krishna.

n5bce5d8d0b9.s: The inscriptions that serve as a source for Satavahana history are written in:
n5bce5d8d0b9.x: Satavahana history rests on the Puranas, coins and Prakrit inscriptions; foreign accounts must be cross-checked with these.

n38909a39bf0.s: Which inscription records Santamula's foundation of the kingdom at Vijayapuri?
n38909a39bf0.x: The Nagarjunakonda inscription records Santamula's foundation of the kingdom; Manchikallu records the Pallava conquest.

nap-history-3-16.s: Which inscription is the first to mention Vishnu temples in Andhra?
nap-history-3-16.x: The Pedavegi inscription first mentions Vishnu temples in Andhra.

n90e7c8fee7b.s: Attirala, where a hoard of Roman gold coins was found, is in which district?
n90e7c8fee7b.x: Roman gold coin hoards were found at Attirala in Kadapa and Vinukonda in Guntur.

n9af0d0e0db2.s: The capital of the Brihatpalayana king Jayavarma was:
n9af0d0e0db2.x: The Kondamudi copper edict names Koduru as Jayavarma's capital.

n9bf9552b8ef.s: The Manchikallu inscription records the conquest of Vijayapuri by Pallava:
n9bf9552b8ef.x: The Manchikallu inscription records Simhavarman's conquest of Vijayapuri.

nfdd28b2b114.s: The Bhattiprolu relic caskets are associated with which pre-Satavahana local ruler?
nfdd28b2b114.x: The caskets belong to the pre-Satavahana ruler Kubiraka; Bhattiprolu is the oldest stupa in AP.

n9105ba0f501.s: The last Ikshvaku ruler Rudrapurushadatta was defeated by:
n9105ba0f501.x: Pallava Simhavarman defeated Rudrapurushadatta; the Pallavas took the land south of the Krishna.

nf35f002e255.s: Gathasaptasati, a Prakrit work of 700 verses, is attributed to:
nf35f002e255.x: Hala's Gathasaptasati is a Prakrit work of 700 verses that records early Telugu words.

n2620d20f01c.s: The Naneghat inscription was issued by:
n2620d20f01c.x: The Naneghat inscription was issued by Queen Naganika, wife of Satakarni I.

nf800c4d45fd.s: Gautami Balasri's Nasik inscription belongs to the reign of:
nf800c4d45fd.x: The Nasik inscription was issued during Vasishthiputra Pulumavi's reign and records Gautamiputra Satakarni's victories.

n7ad61e5e789.s: According to the Matsya Purana, how many Satavahana kings ruled for 456 years?
n7ad61e5e789.x: The Matsya Purana mentions 30 Satavahana kings ruling for 456 years.

n1784132bdc8.s: Which Andhra habitation mound also had a mint?
n1784132bdc8.x: Kondapur is a habitation mound and a mint; Gudiwada Dibba is a Mauryan-to-Satavahana habitation mound.

nap-history-3-5.s: The only inscription about the Brihatpalayanas is the:
nap-history-3-5.x: The Kondamudi copper plate of Jayavarma is the only record of the Brihatpalayanas, who were Ikshvaku feudatories.

nap-history-3-4.s: The Allahabad Pillar inscription of Samudragupta names which ruler of Vengi?
nap-history-3-4.x: The Allahabad Pillar inscription names Hastivarman of Vengi (Salankayana) among the southern kings Samudragupta defeated.

nap-history-3-21.s: The Eluru inscription, which mentions 'Munyada', was issued by:
nap-history-3-21.x: The Eluru inscription was issued by Devavarma; Nandivarman II issued the Kolleru inscription.

o: Military orders from a village council
Land grants to Brahmins, often with tax exemptions
n2db72ec83bc.x: Copper-plate grants generally record a king granting a village or land to Brahmins, with tax exemptions.

nb37f6f6bc8d.s: A table-like megalithic chamber made of large slabs is called a:
nb37f6f6bc8d.x: A dolmen is a table-like chamber; a cist is a stone-slab box, a menhir an upright stone and a sarcophagus a terracotta coffin.

n3ae1ae2d301.s: Upper Palaeolithic cave art at Bhimbetka has been found in about how many caves and shelters?
n3ae1ae2d301.x: Bhimbetka has Upper Palaeolithic art in about 300 caves and shelters.

nindian-history-137-9.s: Ahar is the type site of which Chalcolithic culture?
nindian-history-137-9.x: Ahar is the type site of the Ahar/Banas culture; Inamgaon belongs to the Jorwe culture.

ncb2dc4c8393.s: Yerragondapalem in Andhra Pradesh is known for:
ncb2dc4c8393.x: Yerragondapalem is known for well-made quartzite blades.

n3c50022b20c.s: The microlith centres of Andhra Pradesh were discovered by:
n3c50022b20c.x: Robert Bruce Foote discovered the AP microlith centres; N. R. Banerji is the leading researcher of megaliths.

nf4bd5885343.s: Black-and-red ware was found at all Andhra megalithic sites except:
nf4bd5885343.x: Black-and-red ware was found at all Andhra megalithic sites except Visakhapatnam.

ne9bb546e344.s: The Ahar and Kayatha Chalcolithic cultures were contemporaries of the:
ne9bb546e344.x: Ahar and Kayatha were Harappan contemporaries, though many Chalcolithic cultures were post-Harappan.

need7a8df4b4.s: V. S. Wakankar discovered Bhimbetka in:
need7a8df4b4.x: Bhimbetka was discovered by V. S. Wakankar in 1957 and became a UNESCO site in 2003.

nde9ead6b340.s: The Middle Palaeolithic is principally a ____ stage.
nde9ead6b340.x: The Middle Palaeolithic is principally a flake-tool stage; microliths belong to the Upper Palaeolithic and Mesolithic.

nindian-history-137-16.s: The Chalcolithic site of Kayatha is located in:
nindian-history-137-16.x: Kayatha is in Madhya Pradesh; Jorwe, Savalda and Inamgaon are in Maharashtra.

n189dc615718.s: In 1842 Meadows Taylor found a stone axe at:
n189dc615718.x: Meadows Taylor's 1842 stone axe was found at Lingasugur, not Jwalapuram.

n97b9bff4a05.s: The animal most commonly painted in rock art is the:
n97b9bff4a05.x: The deer, not the elephant, is the most commonly painted animal.

nindian-history-137-14.s: The Jorwe culture, known for village farming settlements, belongs to:
nindian-history-137-14.x: Jorwe belongs to Maharashtra, not Madhya Pradesh.

ncd771fe3160.s: About how many types of megalithic burials have been identified in Andhra Pradesh?
ncd771fe3160.x: About twelve types of megalithic burials are noted in AP, studied by N. R. Banerji.

nb448d1e3b20.s: Handaxes, cleavers and choppers of quartzite and limestone are typical of the:
nb448d1e3b20.x: Handaxes, cleavers and choppers are Lower Palaeolithic tools; flakes are Middle, blades Upper Palaeolithic and microliths Mesolithic.

na79cb04b78a.s: Giddaluru, the key microlithic centre of Andhra Pradesh, is in which district?
na79cb04b78a.x: Giddaluru in Prakasam district is the key microlithic centre, along with Nagarjunakonda, Kondapur and Khammam.

nebdb8934095.s: AMS dating at Mayiladumparai places the beginning of the Iron Age in South India at about:
nebdb8934095.x: Mayiladumparai AMS dating puts the start of the South Indian Iron Age at about 2100 BCE, earlier than the Gangetic Iron Age.

nf4a0b3ec6e3.s: Patapadu in Andhra Pradesh is known for:
nf4a0b3ec6e3.x: Patapadu has Chalcolithic painted pottery; Keesarapalli has copper tools.

n475b789e801.s: Palaeolithic tools from the Kadapa-Kurnool region were mainly made of:
n475b789e801.x: Quartzite was characteristic of Kadapa-Kurnool tools, while limestone was used north of the Krishna.

n8c2548f2860.s: Rhinoceros remains have been found at which Early Harappan site?
n8c2548f2860.x: Amri, which shows a transition from the pre-Harappan to the Mature Harappan phase, has yielded rhinoceros remains.

n7f4943ead5c.s: Who suggested that the Harappan Civilisation arose through migration from Sumer?
n7f4943ead5c.x: Mackay suggested migration from Sumer; Marshall proposed indigenous evolution and Wheeler diffusion from West Asia.

n3dae48589b4.s: The main domesticated animals of the Neolithic phase of Baluchistan and the Indus plains were:
n3dae48589b4.x: The main domesticated animals were sheep and goats, not horses and camels.

nf6fb9afb123.s: Kili Gul Muhammad, an early farming village, lies in which valley?
nf6fb9afb123.x: Kili Gul Muhammad lies in the Quetta valley; Rana Ghundai is in the Zhob-Loralai valley.

n31bf98b6d9b.s: Which of the following was already known in the Early Harappan phase?
n31bf98b6d9b.x: Copper, the wheel and the plough were already known in the Early Harappan phase.

n99ff209adc6.s: Mehrgarh, with the earliest evidence of agriculture in the subcontinent, lies near which pass?
n99ff209adc6.x: Mehrgarh lies in Baluchistan near the Bolan Pass; it begins c. 7000 BCE.

n827f0d70365.s: The pottery of Kalibangan is classified into how many fabrics?
n827f0d70365.x: Kalibangan's pottery is classified into six fabrics; its settlement had a mud-brick fortification.

n0eeb97ef526.s: The Early (Pre-) Harappan phase (3300-2600 BCE) is called the:
n0eeb97ef526.x: The Early Harappan phase is called the Regionalisation Era, not the Integration Era; it corresponds to the Hakra phase.

nded5ae6ec83.s: At Mehrgarh, the dead were usually:
o: Buried under or near houses, flexed, with grave goods
Buried in public monuments without objects
nded5ae6ec83.x: At Mehrgarh the dead were buried under or near houses, often flexed, with ornaments, tools and sometimes goats.

n7ee00b44d4f.s: Which of the following is an Early Harappan regional pottery tradition?
n7ee00b44d4f.x: Kot Diji ware is one of the Early Harappan regional traditions, along with Amri, Sothi-Siswal and Hakra wares.

n8284f071d87.s:
Assertion (A): Dholavira was the first Indus Valley Civilisation site in India to be listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Reason (R): Dholavira became Gujarat's fourth UNESCO World Heritage Site.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n8284f071d87.x: Both are true: Dholavira was the first IVC site in India to be listed and became Gujarat's fourth World Heritage Site, but being Gujarat's fourth does not explain being the first IVC site.

nindian-history-137-19.s: The Harappan settlement of Banawali is in:
nindian-history-137-19.x: Banawali is a Harappan site in Haryana; Rangpur is a Late Harappan site in Gujarat.

n92a81103255.s: The Mature Harappan phase is dated to:
n92a81103255.x: The Mature Harappan phase is 2600-1900 BCE; 1900-1300 BCE is the Late Harappan phase.

n8bb1cab538d.s: The Harappan site of Mandi is in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
n8bb1cab538d.x: Mandi is in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh.

nindian-history-2-11.x: B. P. Bopardikar discovered Daimabad in 1958; Yagyadatt Sharma excavated Ropar and R. S. Bisht Dholavira.

nindian-history-2-4.x: R. D. Banerjee is linked with Mohenjo-daro (1922); Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa (1921).

nindian-history-26-2-5.x: Burzahom is known for pit dwellings; Sinauli for 125 burials and Banawali for a terracotta plough.

nindian-history-3-26.s: The bronze buffalo was found at:
nindian-history-3-26.x: Daimabad yielded the bronze buffalo; Ropar had a dog buried with humans.

n112e027a70b.x: J. P. Joshi excavated Surkotada; R. S. Bisht excavated Banawali and Y. D. Sharma Ropar.

nindian-history-3-58.s: A signboard of ten Indus signs was found at:
nindian-history-3-58.x: The ten-sign signboard is from Dholavira; Lothal has the dockyard and Kalibangan the ploughed field.

nindian-history-2-20.s: The Harappan site of Manda is associated with:
nindian-history-2-20.x: Manda is linked with Himalayan wood; reservoirs belong to Dholavira and bronze objects to Daimabad.

n348801997aa.s: The westernmost Harappan boundary site is:
n348801997aa.x: Sutkagendor is the western boundary site; Manda is northern, Alamgirpur eastern and Daimabad southern.

nindian-history-26-2-20.s: Harappa is situated on the bank of the river:
nindian-history-26-2-20.x: Harappa lies on the Ravi; Mohenjo-daro is on the Indus, Ropar on the Sutlej and Manda on the Chenab.

nindian-history-3-35.s: The earliest evidence of a furnace in the Harappan context comes from:
nindian-history-3-35.x: Kot Bala gives the earliest furnace evidence.

nindian-history-3-28.s: A terracotta toy plough was found at:
nindian-history-3-28.x: Banawali yielded a terracotta replica of a plough (toy plough), along with Mother Goddess figurines.

nindian-history-3-59.x: The Great Bath belongs to Mohenjo-daro, not Lothal.

n246efb13b7f.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is in India (Gujarat)?
n246efb13b7f.x: Lothal is in Gujarat; Harappa, Mohenjodaro and Chanhudaro are in Pakistan.

nindian-history-3-52.s: Skeletons found in wells are associated with:
nindian-history-3-52.x: Skeletons in wells are linked with Mohenjo-daro, along with the humped bull seal.

nindian-history-3-60.s: Evidence of an earthquake has been found at which Harappan site?
nindian-history-3-60.x: Kalibangan shows evidence of an earthquake, besides a ploughed field and fire altars.

nindian-history-3-78.s: Rice, bajra and sorghum are associated with which Harappan site?
nindian-history-3-78.x: Rangpur in Saurashtra yielded rice, bajra and sorghum.

nindian-history-2-5.s: A bead-making factory and furnace were revealed at:
nindian-history-2-5.x: The 1935-36 excavation at Chanhudaro revealed a bead-making factory and furnace.

nindian-history-3-11.x: Daimabad lies on the Pravara, a tributary of the Godavari, not on the Narmada.

nindian-history-3-5.s: Kalibangan lies on the bank of the:
nindian-history-3-5.x: Kalibangan lies on the Ghaggar; the Bhogava is Lothal's river.

nindian-history-3-22.s: A copper dog was found at:
nindian-history-3-22.x: Lothal yielded a copper dog, rice husk, a Persian Gulf seal and three double burials.

n49162fa1537.s: Who first described the ruins of Harappa, during 1826-38?
n49162fa1537.x: Charles Masson described the ruins during 1826-38; Fleet published seals in 1912 and Sahni found Harappa in 1921-22.

nf1c5968b260.x: Mehrgarh is a Neolithic site; Sohgaura is the Mauryan copper-plate site.

nindian-history-3-31.s: Manda, a base for procuring Himalayan wood, lies on the river:
nindian-history-3-31.x: Manda on the Chenab was a base for Himalayan timber floated downstream to other Harappan towns.

n7c18f8cd305.s: The Harappan site of Alamgirpur, on the Hindon, is in which district?
n7c18f8cd305.x: Alamgirpur lies on the Hindon in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh; Kalibangan is in Hanumangarh and Ropar on the Sutlej in Punjab.

nindian-history-3-4.s: The first Harappan site excavated in independent India was:
nindian-history-3-4.x: Ropar (Rupnagar) on the Sutlej in Punjab was the first Harappan site excavated after Independence.

nindian-history-3-77.s: Dholavira had how many urban divisions?
nindian-history-3-77.x: Dholavira had three divisions: Citadel, Middle Town and Lower Town.

nindian-history-3-71.s: Mandi in Muzaffarnagar is known for a Harappan:
nindian-history-3-71.x: Mandi is known for a Harappan jewellery hoard found in 2000.

nindian-history-3-74.s: Shortughai, a Harappan trade outpost for lapis lazuli, is in:
nindian-history-3-74.x: Shortughai is in Afghanistan; Kerala-no-dhoro, a salt centre, is in Gujarat.

n1f265c44627.s: The broad social-economic character attributed to the Rigvedic period is:
n1f265c44627.x: The comparison is Indus Valley - urban, Rigvedic - pastoral, Later Vedic - agrarian and Medieval - landlordism.

n7938cd7a85a.s: The Harappan Civilisation is estimated to have covered about:
n7938cd7a85a.x: It covered about 1.3 million square kilometres and supported about five million people.

n7ef6970d5cc.s: Which of the following was among the five iconic archaeological sites named in the Union Budget of 2020?
n7ef6970d5cc.x: The five sites were Rakhigarhi, Hastinapur, Shivsagar, Dholavira and Adichanallur.

n43ea803cb51.s: The Harappan site of Hulas is in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
n43ea803cb51.x: Hulas is in Saharanpur and Mandi in Muzaffarnagar, both in Uttar Pradesh.

nindian-history-2-7.s: Alexander Cunningham visited Harappa, seeing pottery, tools and a seal, in:
nindian-history-2-7.x: Cunningham was at Harappa in 1853 and 1856 but did not grasp the significance of the remains.

nae3966b7f5e.s: Rakhigarhi is located in which state?
nae3966b7f5e.x: Rakhigarhi is in Haryana, not Rajasthan; Kalibangan is the Rajasthan site.

ndd9dfd80dd8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indus Valley cities?
o: No palaces or temples have been clearly identified in them.
Their drainage was more advanced than that of contemporary Mesopotamia and Egypt.
The absence of palaces or temples proves there was no civic authority.
Their standardised urban planning suggests a civic authority.
ndd9dfd80dd8.x: The absence of clearly identified palaces or temples does not disprove civic authority; standardised planning instead suggests it.

nf7352fe7bfa.s: Which of the following pairs about the Harappan street plan is correctly matched?
o: Direction of streets - north-east to south-west
Crossing of streets - at acute angles
Width of main streets - about 30 metres
Width of main streets - about 10 metres
nf7352fe7bfa.x: Harappan streets ran north-south and east-west, crossed at right angles and divided cities into blocks; main streets were about 30 feet or 10 metres wide.

nd16914cf0b1.s: What was provided in covered Harappan drains for cleaning them?
nd16914cf0b1.x: Covered Harappan drains had manholes for maintenance and used street slopes for natural flow.

n99c4a5defd9.s: Which Harappan site used sandstone and limestone blocks as an exception to brick construction?
n99c4a5defd9.x: Burnt bricks were common and mud bricks were used at Kalibangan; Dholavira was the exception using sandstone and limestone blocks.

ncce3069e3fd.s: Giant reservoirs fed by bunds, check-dams and channels are a feature of:
ncce3069e3fd.x: Dholavira had giant reservoirs supplied through bunds, check-dams and channels, along with dams and embankments.

na53bba7da44.s: At which Harappan site were the citadel and lower town in one enclosure?
na53bba7da44.x: Lothal had both divisions in one enclosure; Kalibangan had a fortified lower town.

nindian-history-3-18.x: Harappa yielded Cemetery H, a coffin burial, wheat and barley in a wooden mortar, and dice.

nindian-history-3-24.s: A stadium-like open ground was found at which Harappan site?
nindian-history-3-24.x: Dholavira had a stadium-like open ground and special cemetery structures besides its reservoirs.

nindian-history-3-46.s: The Harappa granary had how many rooms?
nindian-history-3-46.x: The Harappa granary had two rows of six rooms each, giving 12 rooms.

nced633c9563.s: Unlike baked-brick Mohenjodaro and Harappa, Dholavira used which material for major construction?
nced633c9563.x: Dholavira used sandstone and limestone blocks for major construction, and some reservoirs were partly cut into rock.

nb984eb9d761.s: Harappan granaries are generally interpreted as:
nb984eb9d761.x: Granaries are commonly read as stores of agricultural surplus, though the interpretation is debated.

nadcee85e719.s: Which smaller Harappan settlement lacked a systematic drainage system?
nadcee85e719.x: Banawali lacked a systematic drainage system, while Kalibangan had wooden drains.

n6b226c0aab1.s: Which Harappan site is noted for radial streets?
n6b226c0aab1.x: Banawali is noted for radial streets; Dholavira had three parts and Chanhudaro no citadel.

n19f87cadcc1.s: In Harappan cities, the raised and fortified citadel generally lay on the:
n19f87cadcc1.x: The citadel was a raised, fortified western area with public buildings; the lower town lay to the east.

nb7633684b45.s: Which Harappan site has yielded the largest number of wells?
nb7633684b45.x: Mohenjodaro has the most wells; Dholavira is known for reservoirs rather than wells.

naf5b2c5cda5.s: The red sandstone male torso was found at:
naf5b2c5cda5.x: The red sandstone male torso is from Harappa; the Pashupati seal is from Mohenjodaro and the ship seal from Lothal.

n7213065adee.s: The most common motif on Harappan seals is the:
n7213065adee.x: The unicorn is the most common Harappan seal motif, and the pipal is the most depicted tree.

nb6858b13a3d.s: Which of the following is one of the five largest Harappan cities?
nb6858b13a3d.x: The five largest cities are Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi and Dholavira.

o: An animal motif with an inscription
nc103fdb8efe.x: Rectangular seals carry only inscriptions, while square seals combine an animal motif with an inscription.

n90ddff6943a.s: Shell work in the Harappan civilisation was concentrated at Nageshwar, Balakot and:
n90ddff6943a.x: Shell work was concentrated at Nageshwar, Balakot and Lothal.

nindian-history-38-10.s: Which Harappan crop was connected with textiles and trade?
nindian-history-38-10.x: Cotton was the Harappan textile crop; maize was unknown in India until the Portuguese brought it.

nb3d8c11a0af.s: A copper scale of the Harappan civilisation was found at:
nb3d8c11a0af.x: The copper scale was found at Harappa, the ivory scale at Lothal and the shell scale at Mohenjodaro.

nb7c648254a1.s: Which animal does NOT appear on Harappan seals or figurines?
nb7c648254a1.x: The lion does not appear on Harappan seals or figurines.

nd65d33343f9.s: Evidence of well irrigation in the Harappan civilisation comes from:
nd65d33343f9.x: Well irrigation is evidenced at Allahdino, reservoirs at Dholavira and plough models at Banawali.

n53e2f3aff33.s: Harappan seals, beads and weights are NOT reported from:
n53e2f3aff33.x: They are reported from Oman, Bahrain, Iraq and Iran, but not from Egypt.

n494cbf7df4b.s: The horse bones claimed from Surkotada are dated to approximately:
n494cbf7df4b.x: The Surkotada horse bones are claimed to date to about 2000 BCE, though their identification is controversial.

n974eee00fd4.s: The Harappans obtained lapis lazuli from:
n974eee00fd4.x: Lapis lazuli came from Badakhshan through Shortughai; copper came from Khetri and Oman and gold from Kolar.

nacd6bee9594.s: Indus seals found at Susa, Ur, Nippur, Failaka and Bahrain show Harappan contacts with:
nacd6bee9594.x: These finds at Susa, Ur, Nippur, Failaka and Bahrain demonstrate Harappan contacts with West Asia and the Gulf.

n07510b645de.s: Farm surplus, trade networks, craft specialisation and ____ together created the conditions for Indus urbanisation.
n07510b645de.x: Farm surplus, trade networks, craft specialisation and standard weights together created the conditions for urbanisation.

ne36c1d07099.s: Shortughai, a Harappan colony connected with lapis lazuli supply, is in:
ne36c1d07099.x: Shortughai in Afghanistan supplied lapis lazuli from Badakhshan.

n6d627c87245.s: Which of the following was an import, not an export, of the Harappans?
n6d627c87245.x: Carnelian beads, ivory, timber and cotton were exports; silver was imported.

ndae12627ff6.s: The Greeks referred to cotton as:
ndae12627ff6.x: The Greeks called cotton Sindon; the Harappans pioneered cotton textiles.

n98fed4523f6.s: Harappan spinning is evidenced by the common find of ____ in houses.
n98fed4523f6.x: Spindle-whorls occur widely in houses; no spinning wheels have been found.

n8ca449490c5.s: Chert blades from which site show that stone tools continued alongside metal tools?
n8ca449490c5.x: Chert blades from Rohri show that stone tools continued alongside metal tools; iron was unknown to the Harappans.

n720c71900d4.s: Which agricultural practice did the Harappans follow?
n720c71900d4.x: Harappan agriculture included double cropping, with surplus stored in granaries.

n64756c694a3.s: The Lothal dockyard was excavated by S. R. Rao in:
n64756c694a3.x: S. R. Rao excavated the Lothal dockyard in 1954, not Mortimer Wheeler in 1931.

n46baac9c701.s: Which animal was known to the Harappans only as a wild animal?
n46baac9c701.x: Dog, cat, ass, camel, sheep and goat were domesticated; elephant and tiger were wild animals.

n406ddba3c7b.x: Meluhha referred to the Indus region; Dilmun was Bahrain and Magan Oman or Makran.

ne52ab973376.s: Which metal was unknown to the Harappans?
ne52ab973376.x: Iron was unknown to the Harappans; copper, bronze, gold, silver and lead were used.

na584cf3d969.s: Harappan bronze, used for tools, weapons and the Dancing Girl, was an alloy of copper and:
na584cf3d969.x: Harappan bronze was made by combining copper and tin.

n028a5025450.s: For which form of irrigation in the Indus Valley Civilisation is evidence still inconclusive?
n028a5025450.x: Wells at Allahdino, reservoirs at Dholavira and flood irrigation are evidenced, but canal irrigation remains inconclusive.

n58ea77de544.s: Which animal was not known to the Mature Harappans, according to the accepted view?
n58ea77de544.x: The horse was not known to the Mature Harappans in the accepted view; the Surkotada claims are controversial.

n23f54912793.s: Harappan seals were NOT used for:
n23f54912793.x: Seals were used for authentication, ownership, sealing packages and identity marking, not for minting coins.

nc38866c0efb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Harappan seals?
o: Square seals generally carry an animal figure with an inscription.
Rectangular seals generally carry only an inscription.
Mesopotamian-type cylinder seals were common at all sites.
Most seals were made of steatite.
nc38866c0efb.x: Mesopotamian-type cylinder seals were rare, not common, at Harappan sites.

n96287c57cae.s: The average Harappan inscription contains about how many signs?
n96287c57cae.x: The average inscription has about five signs; around 5,000 inscribed objects are known and the script is undeciphered.

na80530b51f9.s: Harappan weights, mostly of chert, were generally ____ in shape.
na80530b51f9.x: Harappan weights were generally cubical, not spherical.

n3500296503a.s: Harappan seals were mostly made of:
n3500296503a.x: Harappan seals were mostly of steatite and generally square.

n543378b98db.x: R. S. Bisht excavated Dholavira in 1990; it is the only Harappan site on the UNESCO list (2021).

ndd80574848c.s: Which of the following pairs about Harappan settlement layout is correctly matched?
o: Citadel - public buildings and elite areas
Lower town - public buildings and elite areas
ndd80574848c.x: The western citadel contained public and elite areas, while the eastern lower town held commoners' houses.

nfbc4023cf2a.s: The centralised-state view of Harappan polity rests mainly on:
nfbc4023cf2a.x: The centralised-state view rests on uniformity over a huge area; no single capital has been identified.

ndce882ac48e.s: Caste is considered to have crystallised in which period?
ndce882ac48e.x: Caste crystallised in the Later Vedic period; there is no textual evidence of a rigid Harappan caste system.

n759bc1417b1.s: The Harappan 'Priest-King' figure is depicted wearing a:
n759bc1417b1.x: The Priest-King is shown with a shawl; there is no evidence of stitching in Harappan clothing.

n126f1eb48dd.s: Harappan maces, axes and spears were made of:
n126f1eb48dd.x: Harappan weapons were of copper and bronze, few and simple; no horse-drawn chariots are known.

nd6b733d2967.s: A Harappan toy factory has been found at:
nd6b733d2967.x: Chanhudaro had a toy factory; Harappan toys were of terracotta.

n5a0030d5566.s: Lipstick is associated with which Harappan site?
n5a0030d5566.x: Chanhudaro is associated with lipstick; bronze mirrors, ivory combs and collyrium sticks were also used.

ne1a8ca45866.s: Grave goods such as pottery, ornaments and mirrors in Harappan graves indicate:
ne1a8ca45866.x: Such grave goods indicate belief in an afterlife and differences in status, not cremation.

neeb151edec6.s: How many burial types have been reported at Kalibangan?
neeb151edec6.x: Kalibangan has extended burials in rectangular pits, pot burials and circular pits with grave goods but no skeleton.

n672e3135aeb.s: Standardised bricks, binary weights, uniform seals and grid-plan towns over a vast area suggest that the Harappans had:
o: A significant degree of central authority
n672e3135aeb.x: Widespread standardisation is the principal basis for inferring a significant degree of central authority.

n9d9d54c2e79.s: Reconstruction of Harappan social stratification and polity relies mainly on:
n9d9d54c2e79.x: Interpretations rely mainly on material remains, as the script gives no names of rulers.

n89b84e257dc.s: The Harappan political structure, for which there is no clear-cut evidence, has been described as appearing:
o: A centralised empire with one capital
n89b84e257dc.x: The political structure is not clear-cut and has been described as appearing corporate.

n98943488e2e.s: Fractional burial at Mohenjodaro and Harappa involved:
o: Placing ashes in an urn after cremation
Burying bones after exposure of the body
Burying the complete body in a coffin
Burying a human together with a dog
n98943488e2e.x: Fractional burial involved burying the bones after the body had been exposed.

nb967023ce50.s: A gemstone factory with over 3,000 semi-precious stones was found at:
nb967023ce50.x: Rakhigarhi had the gemstone factory; Chanhudaro had a bead-making factory and Lothal bead workshops.

n635e6d376ca.s: Which is the only Indus city without a citadel?
n635e6d376ca.x: Chanhudaro is the only Indus city without a citadel.

ne961d7c9370.s: A Harappan gold foundry with an active furnace was found at:
ne961d7c9370.x: Rakhigarhi had a gold foundry with an active furnace; gold and silver necklaces were found at Allahdino.

n600ae096f7f.x: Carnelian came from Saurashtra, and carnelian beads were exported to Mesopotamia and the Persian Gulf.

naea801bc8e8.s: The lost-wax technique of metal casting is also known as:
naea801bc8e8.x: The lost-wax process, or cire perdue, coats a wax model with clay, melts out the wax and pours molten metal into the mould.

n56ab91358c4.s: Terracotta toy carts with seated drivers were found at:
n56ab91358c4.x: Toy carts with seated drivers come from Chanhudaro.

n1c39d0103ee.s: Differences in house size, burial goods and ornaments in the IVC indicate:
n1c39d0103ee.x: Differences in house size, burial goods and ornaments indicate social stratification; the four-fold division is speculative.

n82fac714ba2.s: The Great Bath at Mohenjodaro is associated with:
n82fac714ba2.x: The Great Bath suggests ritual purification.

n1958af7741f.s: The bronze Dancing Girl was excavated in 1926 by:
n1958af7741f.x: Ernest Mackay excavated the Dancing Girl in 1926 under John Marshall.

ne35f9f60d01.s: Which of the following was known to the Harappans?
ne35f9f60d01.x: Mirrors and combs were known to the Harappans.

n183b181ce69.s: Who identified the figure on the Pashupati seal as Proto-Shiva?
n183b181ce69.x: John Marshall proposed the Proto-Shiva or Pashupati interpretation, which is debated.

n5329ce0b51a.s: Harappan Mother Goddess worship has a later parallel in:
n5329ce0b51a.x: Mother Goddess worship has a later parallel in Shakti or mother-goddess cults.

n3ca805b68c7.x: Harappan religion was nature- and fertility-oriented; Later Vedic religion was sacrificial and ritualistic.

n819fdfb9a8b.s: The pipal motif in the Indus Valley Civilisation goes back to the:
n819fdfb9a8b.x: The pipal motif is traced to the Early Harappan phase and continued in later Indian religion.

nindian-history-42-16.s: The image of Lakshmi appears on the coins of:
nindian-history-42-16.x: Lakshmi appears on Muhammad Ghori's coins.

n8c95b0170bb.s: Mother Goddess figurines and the male Pashupati figure show that the Indus people worshipped:
n8c95b0170bb.x: These finds show worship of both female and male deities.

nindian-history-41-8.s: The entire 9th Mandala of the Rigveda is devoted to:
nindian-history-41-8.x: Soma has the whole 9th Mandala of the Rigveda.

nindian-history-41-14.s: In the Rigveda, Varuna is the upholder of:
nindian-history-41-14.x: Varuna is the upholder of cosmic order; Agni is the god of fire and sacrifice and Indra the warrior god.

nindian-history-41-17.x: Chaitanya preached Krishna Bhakti; Guru Nanak worshipped the formless Nirgun Brahma.

ne027c59323c.s: The proto-Shiva reading of the Pashupati seal is treated cautiously mainly because:
o: The seal is made of gold
The seal was found outside India
The seal is a later forgery
ne027c59323c.x: The undeciphered script is a principal reason why the proto-Shiva interpretation remains debated.

n343368fdaf8.s: The Harappan fire altars cannot be treated as conclusive evidence of:
n343368fdaf8.x: Their link with fire worship or yajna and resemblance to Vedic ritual spaces remain debated.

n394e38d5312.s: Rig Vedic religion was centred on:
o: Male nature gods and open-air yajnas
n394e38d5312.x: Rig Vedic religion featured male nature gods like Indra, Agni and Varuna and open-air yajnas, with no temples or idols.

n5b668b83b8d.s: The current consensus explains the Harappan decline as:
n5b668b83b8d.x: The consensus rejects a single sudden catastrophe and favours a gradual, multi-causal decline.

n7f557f8a10e.s: Pollen evidence from Deoria Tal in Uttarakhand indicates that during the 4.2 ka event the monsoon:
n7f557f8a10e.x: The Deoria Tal evidence indicates a sharp weakening of the monsoon.

nec62895709b.s: Which Harappan site was flooded several times?
nec62895709b.x: Chanhudaro was flooded several times, and the shifting Indus led to the abandonment of Mohenjodaro.

n18822f8e532.s: Which of the following was absent in the Mature Harappan phase and became important only later?
n18822f8e532.x: Horse, chariot and iron were absent in the Mature Harappan phase; fire altars, pipal worship and burials are cited as continuities.

n34b8a3a2aa7.s: The invasion theory of the Harappan decline, now rejected, was put forward by:
n34b8a3a2aa7.x: Wheeler's invasion theory is rejected for lack of archaeological evidence and the reinterpretation of the skeletons.

nff24e48ee82.s: Which change occurred during the Late Harappan phase?
nff24e48ee82.x: In the Late Harappan phase seals, script and weights declined, long-distance trade weakened and bricks lost uniformity.

nfc3aba08290.s: The shift of the Indus course as a cause of the Harappan decline is associated with:
nfc3aba08290.x: H. T. Lambrick is linked with the Indus shift; Fairservis with ecological imbalance and Agrawal and Sood with Ghaggar-Hakra drying.

ndd3ad119841.s: Which of the following is cited as an ecological stress behind the Harappan decline?
ndd3ad119841.x: Deforestation, soil salinity, overgrazing and exhaustion of copper and timber are cited as ecological and resource stresses.

nc1ed30ad479.s: In the Late Harappan phase, pottery became:
nc1ed30ad479.x: Late Harappan cultures developed more regionally varied pottery, while stone and copper tools continued.

n83d2eff27d6.s: The flood theory of the Harappan decline is associated with:
o: Aurel Stein and A. N. Ghosh
Marshall, Mackay and S. R. Rao
n83d2eff27d6.x: Marshall, Mackay and S. R. Rao are linked with floods; Wheeler, Childe and Piggott with invasion; Lambrick with the Indus shift.

n2b9289271de.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Harappan settlement - urban and planned cities
Rigvedic horse - domesticated and central to warfare
Rigvedic armour - coat of mail and helmet
n2b9289271de.x: The horse was central to Rigvedic, not Harappan, warfare; Harappan cultural transmission is associated with seals and script.

n05464b4d5ba.s: Which scholar is a proponent of the indigenous or 'Out of India' theory?
n05464b4d5ba.x: S. R. Rao, B. B. Lal and Shrikant Talageri back the indigenous theory; Max Muller, Wheeler and Parpola back migration.

n7942db5de8a.s: The Swat valley culture known for horse remains and new burial practices is the:
n7942db5de8a.x: The Swat valley culture is the Gandhara Grave culture; BMAC lay in Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and north Afghanistan.

n29881829ce8.s: Which animal was domesticated and central to Rigvedic warfare, but is not attested in the Harappan civilisation?
n29881829ce8.x: The Rigvedic horse was domesticated and central to warfare; no awareness of the horse is attributed to the Harappans.

nf20112d7ae3.s: The oldest Iranian (Zoroastrian) text is the:
nf20112d7ae3.x: The Avesta is the oldest Iranian Zoroastrian text and closely parallels the Rigveda.

nc67430db23d.s: Which genetic haplogroup is discussed in relation to the Aryan migration theory?
nc67430db23d.x: The migration theory draws on linguistics, Rigvedic geography, horse and chariot archaeology and genetics, including the R1a haplogroup.

nc84bb0686b2.s: According to Iranian literature, the Dasas were:
o: A branch of the early Aryans
nc84bb0686b2.x: The Dasas were regarded as a branch of the early Aryans, while the Dasyus were original inhabitants.

nd4b9f1436c0.s: The Dardic branch of the Indo-European languages is associated with:
nd4b9f1436c0.x: Dardic is associated with Jammu and Kashmir; Iranian is found outside India.

n605faa85713.s: The Boghazkoi inscription records a peace treaty between the Hittites and the rulers of:
n605faa85713.x: Boghazkoi records a Hittite-Mitanni treaty invoking Indra, Mitra, Varuna and the Nasatyas, c. 14th century BCE.

ndd73861c963.s: Who located the original home of the Aryans in Tibet?
ndd73861c963.x: Dayananda Saraswati associated the homeland with Tibet in Satyarth Prakash.

nc1d864e8ccc.s: B. B. Lal linked which pottery with the Vedic tradition?
nc1d864e8ccc.x: B. B. Lal identified the Sarasvati with the Rigvedic river and linked Painted Grey Ware with the Vedic tradition.

nf2c028951a9.x: Harappans used solid wheels; spoked-wheel chariots are part of the migration argument.

nccaebeafaf9.s: Which steppe culture, associated with horses and chariots, is linked to Indo-Iranian speakers?
nccaebeafaf9.x: Andronovo represents steppe pastoralists with horses and chariots linked to Indo-Iranian speakers.

n8efada0cec3.s: The concept of 'Aryan' was popularised in modern scholarship by:
n8efada0cec3.x: Max Muller popularised the concept; it denotes a linguistic-cultural group, not a biologically superior race.

ne0caf4b184d.s: The link between Painted Grey Ware archaeology and ____ remains an open question.
ne0caf4b184d.x: The relationship between Painted Grey Ware and Later Vedic textual geography remains an open question.

n4d056a0a937.s: Which tribe emerged dominant after the Battle of Ten Kings?
n4d056a0a937.x: The Bharatas emerged dominant; the defeated Purus later allied with them to form the Kurus.

nd6109bca762.s: The Early Vedic geographical core lay in:
nd6109bca762.x: The Early Vedic core lay in Punjab-Haryana; the Later Vedic core shifted east to the Doab, eastern UP and Bihar.

n4792797172a.x: Dhanva means desert land; Himavant is the Himalayas and Mujavant a Hindu Kush mountain associated with Soma.

n18c9ff757c7.s: The river mentioned most often in the Rigveda is the:
n18c9ff757c7.x: The Sindhu (Indus) is the most mentioned river; 'naditama' refers to the Sarasvati.

n229cb967aa7.s: In the Battle of Ten Kings, the Bharata chief Sudas was supported by:
n229cb967aa7.x: Sudas, Bharata chief of the Tritsu family, was supported by Vasishtha, not Vishvamitra.

n4f28dac32de.s: The Rigvedic river Kubha is identified with the modern:
n4f28dac32de.x: Kubha, Krumu, Gomati and Suvastu are the Kabul, Kurram, Gomal and Swat rivers.

nf8930995c2b.s: By tradition, the Battle of Ten Kings arose from the rivalry between:
nf8930995c2b.x: Tradition traces the battle to the rivalry between the priests Vasishtha and Vishvamitra.

nindian-history-16-4.s: Madhya Desh was the region between the Himalayas and the:
nindian-history-16-4.x: Madhya Desh was the region between the Himalayas and the Vindhyas; Aryavarta was northern India.

n3882a75350a.s: Which tribe was one of the Panchajana of the Rigvedic period?
n3882a75350a.x: The Panchajana were the Yadus, Turvasas, Anus, Druhyus and Purus; the Kikatas lay outside it.

n255f5b093f1.s: Which assembly is mentioned most often in the Rigveda?
n255f5b093f1.x: Vidatha is mentioned 122 times, against 9 for the Samiti and 8 for the Sabha.

n6a0aecad305.x: Divodasa, the Bharata chief, defeated Sambara.

n9080223d028.s: The early Vedic Rajan was known by the title:
n9080223d028.x: The Rajan was called Gopati or Gopajanasya, protector of the tribe and its cattle.

nb9f98b49688.s: Women members of the early Vedic Sabha were called:
nb9f98b49688.x: Female members of the Sabha were called Sabhavati; women also attended the Vidatha.

naffcedd88a9.s: The ratnins and regular taxes are features of which period?
naffcedd88a9.x: The Later Vedic period saw hereditary territorial kingship, ratnins, regular taxes and royal sacrifices.

nfffec6ee3f2.s: In the early Vedic polity, the Vrajapati was the:
o: Officer in charge of pasture land
nfffec6ee3f2.x: Vrajapati was the pasture officer; Spasa was the spy, Senani the commander and Purohita the chief priest.

ndd12c7521e3.s: The early Vedic Sena was a:
ndd12c7521e3.x: The Sena was a temporary militia of able-bodied tribesmen; there was no permanent standing army.

n60ae09aa544.s: The Rigvedic river Vipas is the modern:
n60ae09aa544.x: Vipas is the Beas; Sutudri is the Sutlej and Drishadvati the Chautang.

n0f5956e1262.s: Which river was called 'Naditama' in the Rigveda?
n0f5956e1262.x: The Sarasvati was the most sacred river, called Naditama; the Sindhu was the most mentioned.

n2b06e08afe0.s: The Rigvedic river Parushni is the modern:
n2b06e08afe0.x: Parushni is the Ravi; Vitasta is the Jhelum and Asikni the Chenab.

n41c594a2e77.s: Early Vedic weapons were made of:
n41c594a2e77.x: Early Vedic weapons were of bronze, not iron; warriors used a coat of mail and helmet.

n784d3a9977d.s: The word 'Andhra' first appears in the Aitareya Brahmana in the story of:
n784d3a9977d.x: 'Andhra' first appears in the Aitareya Brahmana in connection with the Sunahshepa story, not in the Rig Veda.

nindian-history-16-14.x: Matetama means best of mothers; Devitama means best of goddesses and Naditama best of rivers.

nb40eb1b31a8.s: Which of the following is one of the seven rivers of Sapta Sindhu?
nb40eb1b31a8.x: The standard Sapta Sindhu list is Sindhu, Vitasta, Asikni, Parushni, Vipas, Sutudri and Sarasvati.

n7c1449b8577.x: Samudra means a collection or body of water and does not necessarily denote the sea.

n78477805c69.s: In the Rigvedic period, the head of the family was called:
n78477805c69.x: The family head was the Kulapa or Kulapati; Vrajapati was the pasture officer and Ugra and Jivagribha police officials.
